text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Central Bank to be asked to investigate possible conflict of interest involving chairman of Bank of Valletta. The bank was privatised three years ago but the chairman is still appointed by the government in view of its 25 percent stake. Finance Minister Leo Brincat announced the investigation in reply to a parliamentary question by an MP referring to reports that the chairman had a personal interest in companies that carried out feasibility studies for firms before they asked for bank loans.

- Female bus driver finds male bastion she cannot breach. Doris Balzan, 34, say she has all the qualifications to drive buses and coaches but has been turned down by bus operators because she is a woman.

- Nationalist Party formally applies for television licence. The opposition party has told the Broadcasting Authority that it should issue it with a broadcasting licence in the same way as a licence was issued to the Labour Party four years ago.
